report:
**Conclusion:** No—reliable evidence does not show that ivermectin lowers the risk of death from COVID-19.

The most trustworthy evidence is from randomized controlled trials and systematic reviews, rather than small observational studies. Cochrane’s review found **no evidence supporting ivermectin** for treating COVID-19 or preventing SARS‑CoV‑2 infection. The large TOGETHER randomized trial likewise found that ivermectin did **not** reduce COVID-19 progression requiring hospital admission or prolonged emergency observation; it did not establish a mortality benefit. Because deaths were uncommon in many outpatient trials, this means the evidence does not demonstrate a death-risk reduction—not that a tiny effect can be absolutely excluded.

Ivermectin remains useful for certain parasitic infections when prescribed appropriately, but it is not an established COVID-19 treatment. Avoid veterinary formulations or self-treatment: incorrect dosing can cause serious toxicity. For COVID-19, use clinician-guided, evidence-based care, particularly if you are at high risk of severe illness.

Sources:  
- Cochrane review: https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD015017_ivermectin-preventing-and-treating-covid-19  
- TOGETHER randomized trial (NEJM): https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2115869  
- Trial full text (PubMed Central): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9006771/
